heading: Induction heads emerge abruptly with early in-context learning gains and a loss bump
definition: induction heads appear abruptly in a narrow window early in training, at the same time as a sharp gain in in-context learning and a bump in the loss curve.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce abrupt induction-head emergence alongside gains in in-context learning or synthetic-task accuracy, but do not establish that a bump in training loss occurs at the same time. In the model Vanilla 1B, the sudden learning gain is absent on non-extractive samples, where the answer cannot be copied from context.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy: R2 for abrupt induction-progress and task-accuracy transitions, with the loss bump and token-index ICL gain untested (arXiv:2312.03002#R1, arXiv:2312.03002#R4, arXiv:2312.03002#R5). <1B: R2 for early induction emergence coincident with ICL-score improvement in two-layer GPT2 and Pythia-70M/160M/410M (arXiv:2502.18802#r1, arXiv:2502.18802#r2, arXiv:2502.18802#r3, arXiv:2502.18802#r4, arXiv:2502.18802#r5); loss-bump coincidence untested. 1-10B: R2 for early prefix-matching emergence and all-sample token-loss-difference improvement in Vanilla 1B (arXiv:2511.05743#R1, arXiv:2511.05743#R10), with a scope limit: no sudden phase shift on non-extractive samples (arXiv:2511.05743#R13, verdict limits_scope). All three rows come from one study with one seed per main condition, whose source check was a partial read. 10-100B: ? for the complete claim; coverage exists in counts: versions.V2.studies_by_size, which does not establish replication. >100B: ?; counts: versions.V2.studies_by_size has no >100B key.
suggested_status.reason:
Independent reproductions give R2 for specified components and evaluation conditions: abrupt early prefix-matching emergence alongside sudden all-sample token-loss-difference improvement in Vanilla 1B (arXiv:2511.05743#R1, arXiv:2511.05743#R10), induction/ICL co-timing in pretrained GPT2 and Pythia (arXiv:2502.18802#r1, arXiv:2502.18802#r2, arXiv:2502.18802#r3, arXiv:2502.18802#r4, arXiv:2502.18802#r5), and induction-progress/task-accuracy co-timing in a synthetic two-layer attention-only network (arXiv:2312.03002#R1, arXiv:2312.03002#R4, arXiv:2312.03002#R5). These results do not establish the complete synchronized loss-bump claim.

Vanilla 1B shows no sudden token-loss-difference phase shift when evaluation is restricted to non-extractive samples (arXiv:2511.05743#R13). This is stated as a scope limit, not C. Its verdict record on V2 is limits_scope: the ICL gain that coincides with the phase change reflects copying-type positions only. The same model shows the sudden all-sample gain (arXiv:2511.05743#R10), so this is not a failed replication, and no verdict records an artifact argument. V2.against[4] labels the group challenges after the checker's correction. The rules define no condition-specific C, so whether such a result gives C is for Iris to rule across all versions. R13 also rests on one seed per main condition, with two supplemental seeds that differ in precision and hardware. The study's source check was a partial read, and a full re-read is pending.

OLMo 1B has at least three induction-selective heads by 23B training tokens, establishing early presence; abruptness and coincidence with ICL and loss changes remain undetermined (arXiv:2606.02378#r2). Continued head recruitment limits a single-window account of final circuit membership, while leaving initial abruptness unresolved (arXiv:2606.02378#r18, arXiv:2606.02378#r19, arXiv:2606.02378#r20, arXiv:2606.02378#r21, arXiv:2606.02378#r22, arXiv:2606.02378#r23, arXiv:2606.02378#r24, arXiv:2606.02378#r25, arXiv:2606.02378#r26).

The supplied counts record versions.V2.verdicts.supports.studies = 29, versions.V2.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 16 and versions.V2.verdicts.challenges.studies = 0. These are the script's recorded totals, preceding the checker's label corrections; zero recorded challenges cannot describe the corrected evidence. Counts: versions.V2.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0.
suggested_status.open_questions: Dense-checkpoint natural-language pretraining measurements jointly tracking head formation, token-index ICL and training loss would test the complete coincidence claim. Repeated non-extractive evaluation during formation, across seeds, would establish whether the scope limit in arXiv:2511.05743#R13 persists. A full re-read of arXiv:2511.05743 is needed before Iris weighs it: the R13 passage and Figure 5, Figure 7, and the Appendix G supplemental seeds. Suppose Iris rules that a condition-specific challenge gives C, and the re-read confirms R13. Then the unqualified claim would move to C, while R2 stays for reproduced components. A failed replication of the all-sample co-timing, or a credible artifact argument against it, would also give C. Direct head-onset measurements at 10-100B and above 100B would resolve the larger-scale status.

source.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads

original_result.setup: The original study tracked induction-head scores, loss at different positions in the context, and training loss in 34 decoder-only Transformers.
original_result.result: Induction heads appeared abruptly at approximately 2.5–5 billion training tokens, while the loss advantage for later tokens over earlier tokens rose from under 0.15 to roughly 0.4 nats. In the same window, the loss curve showed a small bump, described as a visibly steeper improvement.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Induction progress coincided with abrupt in-context accuracy gains in full and minimal models.
Each induction head formed as later-token loss fell relative to earlier-token loss.
Across Pythia scales, induction heads emerged early at similar points in training.
Attention to earlier matches’ next tokens increased as later-token loss fell relative to earlier-token loss.
In a two-layer attention model, induction-related loss dropped suddenly after a plateau.
A rapid switch from unigram to bigram predictions accompanied induction-head formation.
Induction heads emerged as loss suddenly dropped after an accuracy plateau.
An early prefix-matching peak coincided with sudden improvement in the all-sample ICL measure.
Repeated-noun retrieval improved early and plateaued within a small fraction of Pythia training.
During early Pythia pretraining, copying performance jumped abruptly.
Early attention increases to earlier matches’ next tokens coincided with the sharpest measured in-context learning improvements.
A two-layer transformer showed a characteristic bump in training loss.
In a disentangled transformer, induction-head emergence accompanied a training-loss drop.
In GPT2, induction-related measures changed abruptly at approximately the same training point.
During transitive inference training, induction strength rose sharply as in-context loss dropped abruptly.
With sufficiently long sequences or large vocabularies, associative-recall accuracy rose sharply as induction attention sharpened.
Pythia induction scores rose sharply as in-context learning accuracy began improving.
Within one early Pythia checkpoint stage, induction scores and copying improved sharply.
Previous-token behavior jumped early; induction behavior and a measure approximating in-context learning followed.
Induction scores jumped alongside sharp test-loss drops in default and easy match-and-copy tasks.
On hierarchical synthetic data, induction-related attention rose sharply early in training.
In autoregressive and masked diffusion models, induction strengthened abruptly early in training.
Pythia induction scores transitioned sharply early; interventions shifted induction strength and in-context learning together.
In Pythia and OLMo, in-context learning and induction mechanisms began at similar training points.
A spectral measure of induction-class heads rose early, within a narrow training window.
Induction-circuit completion coincided with rising attention to earlier matches’ next tokens and falling later-minus-earlier token loss.
On toy data, transformers showed a qualitative phase transition in training loss.
Repeated-block prediction loss fell as induction scores transitioned sharply.
Across three architectures, induction circuits appeared within the first few percent of training.
Individual induction heads began contributing to in-context learning several thousand training steps apart.
Long-range copying accuracy surged late, well after training loss stabilized.
Induction heads became functional through two separate task-accuracy jumps.
Positions requiring tokens absent from context showed no abrupt in-context learning improvement during induction’s phase change.
The smallest Pythia models developed repeated-noun retrieval more gradually.
Token translation developed gradually instead of sharing copying's abrupt early improvement.
Learning longer n-gram patterns took several separate abrupt transitions, each aligned with attention shifts.
A GRU exhibited a similar loss transition despite lacking induction heads.
Loss reduction followed induction-head progress rather than occurring simultaneously.
Reported sharp transitions involved sufficiently long sequences or large vocabularies.
In the study’s baseline transformer, the induction circuit emerged gradually.
Loss fell sharply after the model shifted from selecting wrong information to selecting right information.
Few-shot in-context learning accuracy continued improving gradually after induction scores plateaued.
Harder match-and-copy tasks and suboptimal learning rates produced later, more gradual transitions.
Previous-token heads began forming before the induction circuit reached completion.
Induction circuits continued recruiting their final heads long after initial formation.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Temporally resolved alignment of a training-loss bump with induction-head formation in natural-language pretrained Pythia, OLMo and GPT-2-class models, outside the original. Available rows report validation loss (arXiv:2502.18802#r6), training-loss stabilization after 5B tokens in 162M Llama (arXiv:2409.09281#r2), and a steady power-law decline in OLMo-1B (arXiv:2603.06592#R8). These do not establish bump timing relative to head formation. The Llama copying surge also does not establish induction-head onset or its coincidence with an ICL gain (arXiv:2409.09281#r1/#r3).
untested.basis: The cited rows and their checker assessments leave these timing relationships unresolved. counts: versions.V2.rows_by_state.cannot_determine = 16 is aggregate coverage, not a count specifically of loss-bump tests.

untested.what: A resolved demonstration outside the original that abrupt induction-head formation in a narrow early window, a sharp ICL gain and a loss bump coincide in one run. arXiv:2402.02364 places prefix-matching growth and the ICL-score drop in LM4 (arXiv:2402.02364#R7, arXiv:2402.02364#R8, arXiv:2402.02364#R10); Appendix E qualitatively discusses a bump after the LM3 LLC decrease, without establishing abruptness, narrowness or exact coincidence of all components. Other cited results leave the bump untested (arXiv:2502.18802#r1, arXiv:2502.18802#r5), head formation unmeasured (arXiv:2505.18373#r2), or both head formation and the bump untested (arXiv:2411.07075#R8).
untested.basis: Checker correction for arXiv:2402.02364#R10 and V2.untested[1], together with the cited studies' untested-parts lines. counts: versions.V2.rows_by_state and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.measurement summarize coverage but do not encode simultaneous measurement of all V2 components.

untested.what: Head-level formation timing above 10B parameters, and any test above 100B. The only 10-100B rows are behavioural copying in Pythia-12B.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V2.studies_by_size has no '>100B' key and '10-100B': 2. The 10-100B rows are arXiv:2411.07075#R8 and arXiv:2505.11004#r16/#r18, both behavioural. counts: versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.measurement.by_size.

wording_issues.phrase: a bump in the loss curve
wording_issues.issue: A bump-type loss feature is reported in a toy setting (arXiv:2505.18373 r2, figure only). A loss-transition signature also appears in its two-layer GRU, which cannot implement induction heads (r5); this does not test V2's temporal coincidence. arXiv:2603.06592 reports a loss plateau and drop without induction heads in its N-gram-data model (R7), and a steady power-law training-loss decline in OLMo-1B (R8). Synthetic studies describe a plateau followed by a sudden drop rather than a bump (arXiv:2404.07129 r2; arXiv:2602.07562 R5, test MSE plateau-drop-plateau).

Early presence and recall of final-checkpoint heads are different milestones. arXiv:2606.02378 reports 67% final-circuit recall at 6B tokens, approximately 2.0% of training, in Pythia 1B, and at 10B tokens, approximately 0.3%, in OLMo 1B. The first ≥3-head milestone is approximately 6B and 23B tokens, respectively. arXiv:2502.14010 reports a sharp induction-score rise around step 1,000 of 143,000 in Pythia. arXiv:2409.09281's 162M Llama copying surge at 15B tokens establishes late task mastery, not late induction-head onset or its timing relative to the ICL gain. In the synthetic setting of arXiv:2410.11474, formation follows a plateau with duration Theta((alpha*+1)^2 L log(1/sigma_init)/w*^2).

Initial appearance and completion of the final circuit need separate timing measures. Final-circuit heads keep joining through 80B tokens in Pythia 1B, 3048B in OLMo 1B and 1677B in OLMoE (arXiv:2606.02378). Two induction heads form several thousand steps apart in arXiv:2410.02984. Circuit formation begins in LM3 and completes in LM4 in lw:Zza9MNA7YtHkzAtit, but numerical window width and within-stage timing are unstated; this does not establish a broad appearance window. arXiv:2510.09340 reports 20% accuracy at epoch 30, 60% at epoch 50 and convergence around epoch 65. That two-stage behavioral trajectory qualifies V2 and supports V7's staging claim.

wording_issues.phrase: a sharp gain in in-context learning
wording_issues.issue: Sharp gains occur in all-sample token-loss difference (arXiv:2511.05743 R10) and literal copying (arXiv:2505.11004 r16). For Vanilla 1B, token-loss difference on non-extractive samples explicitly shows no sudden phase shift (arXiv:2511.05743 R13), challenging V2's abrupt-gain prediction in that condition. Token translation develops gradually (arXiv:2505.11004 r17), as does few-shot task accuracy long after induction scores plateau (arXiv:2502.14010 R11). Abrupt behavioral copying development does not itself establish induction-head formation; that correspondence in arXiv:2505.11004 is conjectural.

Co-timing holds at coarse resolution: in Pythia and OLMo, the ICL-onset to mechanism-onset ratio is 0.93-0.97 (arXiv:2607.27281). Loss reduction is delayed after the progress measures in a standard attention-only transformer (arXiv:2511.01033 R8). Associative-recall accuracy improves slightly later than prefix matching and logit attribution in GPT2 125M (arXiv:2511.16893 R3): partial temporal coincidence, without establishing separate head-formation sub-steps. In Pythia-160m/410m, previous-token behavior rises first; induction behavior, the ICL proxy and wiring follow within 1-4B tokens (arXiv:2607.06621). This is observed co-window formation for V2; whether formation comprises separate transitions remains undetermined.

Abruptness varies by setting. The control circuit emerges gradually in a 3M-parameter Pile transformer (arXiv:2510.12071 r2); head formation around step 7k and the induction-score peak at step 9k describe different events. Harder GMC tasks produce later and more gradual transitions (arXiv:2602.07562 R9), qualifying V2. arXiv:2505.17863 reports sharp transitions for sufficiently long sequences and/or large vocabularies, without establishing non-sharp transitions in all remaining settings. In Pythia, the jump is resolved only to one public-checkpoint stage (arXiv:2609.19000 R5).

Timing rows can measure attention patterns rather than composition or copying (arXiv:2511.16893 R1; arXiv:2407.10827 R1; arXiv:2603.06592 R3). Pythia 12B retrieval measurements in arXiv:2411.07075 R8 are behavioral. Its training-token range is 10^6 to 10^11, with initialized and final checkpoints included; behavioral retrieval rises after about 1B tokens and plateaus at approximately 4B. These measurements do not directly time head formation.

method_sensitivity.what: Checkpoint spacing limits timing claims. arXiv:2607.06621 reports previous-token behavior first, followed by induction behavior, the ICL proxy and wiring within 1–4B tokens; spectral percentile versus behavior cannot be ordered at half-doubling resolution. arXiv:2606.02378 finds induction-selective heads in Pythia 1B by approximately 6B tokens, after a sampled revision at 1.1B; OLMoE presence at its first published checkpoint, 20B tokens, upper-bounds formation time. Neither establishes abruptness or ICL/loss coincidence. arXiv:2609.19000's induction jump falls within one public-checkpoint stage. Its Pythia 70m/160m/410m random-sequence copy advantage rises from 0.022 nats at 1.07B tokens to 9.7 nats one stage later; shared batch/context configuration and aligned cliffs are consistent with configuration-dependent timing. arXiv:2402.13055 saves checkpoints every 200 steps; its ICL loss difference decreases quickly from the beginning, and some copying scores rise from 200 steps. These do not establish the complete V2 transition.

arXiv:2402.02364 states that stage boundaries depend on checkpoint spacing, smoothing, differentiation by training time versus log time, and plateau tolerance. arXiv:2410.02984 finds that most full-weight drLLCs respect the original boundaries; some LM3 decreases flatten or shift from 6.5k–8.5k to 5.5k–8k steps. Dataset and estimation changes are confounded; the authors favor changing nβ from 23 to 30 as the explanation. arXiv:2605.24059 times PR=15 crossings among top-30 PR-integral picks in Karpathy GPT-2 124M; induction class is assigned at ≥30× selectivity. This spectral threshold does not establish induction-behavior onset or V2's coincidences. arXiv:2502.18802 defines the transition by a prefix-score threshold, not a slope analysis.

Whether an ICL gain looks sharp depends on the measure. In arXiv:2511.05743's Vanilla 1B model, all-sample token-loss difference shows a sudden improvement, while the non-extractive-sample measure has no sudden phase shift, challenging V2's abrupt-gain prediction for that condition. In arXiv:2505.11004's Pythia-12B, literal-copying accuracy and log probability jump between steps 512 and 1000, while token translation develops gradually; correspondence with head formation is conjectural. arXiv:2502.14010 reports coincident onset of induction and few-shot accuracy improvement, followed by gradual accuracy gains, and differences between few-shot accuracy and token-loss difference. arXiv:2402.13055 reports emergence times that differ by ICL task difficulty.

Synthetic-task settings shift timing and sharpness. arXiv:2602.07562: higher c and higher T/din make transitions later and more gradual. arXiv:2505.17863 reports sharp transitions for sufficiently long sequences and/or large vocabularies, without establishing the converse; emergence time increases with sequence length and vocabulary size. arXiv:2410.11474: plateau duration scales as Theta((alpha*+1)^2 L log(1/sigma_init)/w*^2). arXiv:2402.11004: qualitative stages persist across seeds, but transition position varies, and transition speed depends on the transition-matrix distribution. Its rapid induction-associated second drop in test KL divergence follows a long unigram plateau, qualifying V2's early-training clause; a training-loss bump and token-index ICL gain remain untested.

arXiv:2409.09281 reports that long-range copying development in 162M Llama varies with batch size, learning rate, attention dropout and weight decay; this does not establish induction-head onset or its coincidence with ICL gains. Larger batches slow copying in token terms. arXiv:2409.10559 finds different selector dynamics under stage-split and joint training: joint training first favors an incorrect information set, followed by correct-selector dominance and a sharp last-token cross-entropy drop. These do not measure the compound V2 transition. arXiv:2602.07562 finds smaller learning rates delay the loss drop, larger rates cause instability, and suboptimal hyperparameters can prevent convergence; more gradual transitions are explicitly associated with task difficulty. arXiv:2410.11474 reports different outcomes under GD and Adam in one experiment.

As a baseline, the original reports that one-layer models form no induction heads and that smeared keys let one-layer models develop ICL and shift its timing earlier in two-layer models; the presented smeared-key experiments cover one- and two-layer models only. lw:tiEgivi7crHSnSrH5: parallel and sequential one-layer attention differ; initial induction formation in the sequential model is followed by refinement and a small later ripple, while the two-layer model has a later sharp transition. arXiv:2508.12837: attention-only models show successive stages, while the MLP-layer model has one intermediate plateau; token-index ICL and a coincident loss bump are untested. arXiv:2607.06621: formation timing changes with the positional scheme and spectral constraints.

Timing is similar across Pythia 70M-2.8B (arXiv:2407.10827) and around step 1,000 in all Pythia models (arXiv:2502.14010). But the smallest Pythia models (14M, 31M) rise more slowly in behavioural copying (arXiv:2411.07075). For Pythia 160M, repeated-noun retrieval rises after about 1B tokens and plateaus around 4B over the 10^6–10^11-token evaluation range; this behavioural measure does not determine head onset. arXiv:2607.27281 reports that its few-shot label-induction skill depends on model size.

First-milestone and per-head measures track different events. In arXiv:2606.02378, the first ≥3-head milestone establishes early induction-head presence, without resolving abruptness, formation-window width or ICL/loss coincidence; full final-circuit recall comes at 80B–3048B tokens across the studied models. In arXiv:2410.02984, per-head ICL contributions arise several thousand steps apart, while the joint-head critical point coincides with the end of the ICL-score drop.

method_sensitivity.factor: autoregressive versus masked-diffusion setup and depth
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2607.15893: one-layer attention-only autoregressive and masked-diffusion models stay near zero induction score; two- and three-layer models show abrupt induction emergence after roughly 8–24k of 250k steps, using three-seed averages. Masked-diffusion models transition earlier than matched autoregressive models. Training objective and causal versus bidirectional attention change together, so their separate contributions are not isolated. Coincident token-index ICL gain and a loss bump remain untested.

method_sensitivity.factor: copying mastery and loss signatures versus head onset
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2409.09281: in a 12-layer 162M Llama (batch size 64 per GPU; three-seed copying averages), long-range random-token copying stays low until 10B tokens and surges at 15B. Training loss stabilizes after 5B tokens; ICL score stabilizes at -0.5 nats around 4,000 steps (about 1.85B tokens). No loss bump is reported; induction-head onset and coincidence are undetermined. arXiv:2505.18373: a two-layer GRU on Wonka–Dursley data has a transformer-like training-curve phase-transition signature (figure only); authors say it cannot implement induction heads, so V2 coincidence is untested. arXiv:2603.06592: Figure 6 attributes an initial loss plateau and two later drops to an N-gram-trained 17M LLaMA-based Transformer with absent induction emergence; prose elsewhere gives conflicting loss descriptions. V2 does not require loss-signature exclusivity.

status_amendment.public_note: The phase-change claim's suggested status moves from contested to independently reproduced, with a stated limit. In one 1B model, the sudden in-context-learning gain did not appear when only positions that cannot be copied were scored; that single-seed result is now treated as a limit on the claim rather than a failed replication, pending a full re-read of the study.
status_amendment.level_changed_because: C to R2. The C rested only on arXiv:2511.05743#R13: no sudden token-loss-difference shift on non-extractive samples in Vanilla 1B, one seed per main condition. Its verdict record on V2 is limits_scope. The same model shows the sudden all-sample gain (arXiv:2511.05743#R10), so R13 is neither a failed replication nor an artifact argument, the only two grounds the rules give for C. The study's source check was also a partial read, so this one result cannot carry a whole-version C. Under the written rules the evidence supports R2 with a stated scope limit. V5 and V6 likewise keep an overall R2 despite their challenges labels. If Iris later sets a rule that condition-specific challenges give C, V2 should be re-statused after a full re-read of arXiv:2511.05743.
